subject: Trust account diversions begin — Pinnacle Legal Partners
summary: First of 47 unauthorised transfers from client trust accounts totalling $480,000 over 22 months
content: Thomas Nguyen, Senior Accountant at Pinnacle Legal Partners (Sydney CBD), begins a systematic scheme to divert client trust funds. Using his administrator access to the firm's LEAP practice management system, Nguyen creates fictitious disbursement entries — falsely coded as 'counsel fees' and 'search fees' — and transfers funds to two shell company accounts he controls: Coastal Advisory Pty Ltd (ABN 44 712 305 891) and TN Consulting Services Pty Ltd (ABN 61 830 112 447). The scheme exploits a gap in the firm's reconciliation process: trust account statements are only reviewed quarterly by an external auditor.

subject: Transfer frequency increases — 3 transactions per week
summary: Nguyen increases transaction frequency following departure of Senior Partner who previously reviewed disbursements
content: Following the retirement of Senior Partner David Hartley, who had informally reviewed large disbursements, Nguyen escalates the scheme. Between August and December 2023, he executes 89 individual transfers ranging from $4,200 to $22,500. To avoid detection, amounts are kept below the $25,000 internal audit threshold. Nguyen also manipulates the LEAP audit trail by back-dating entries and deleting email confirmations from the accounts payable module.

subject: Quarterly audit — BDO Australia flags 23 unreconciled disbursements
summary: External auditor BDO Australia identifies $187,400 in disbursements with no corresponding counsel receipts or court invoices
content: During the January 2024 quarterly trust account audit, BDO Australia forensic accountant Rebecca Okafor identifies 23 disbursement entries coded as 'counsel fees' that cannot be matched to any invoice, barrister's trust receipt, or court payment record. The entries total $187,400. Okafor raises a formal qualified audit report under s255 Legal Profession Uniform Law (NSW). Managing Partner Christine Ellard is notified. Nguyen is placed on immediate paid administrative leave pending investigation. The firm's IT systems are preserved.

subject: Pinnacle Legal Partners notifies NSW Law Society of trust account irregularities
summary: Firm reports suspected trust account fraud under mandatory reporting obligations — Law Society opens file LS-2024-0089
content: Managing Partner Christine Ellard lodges a mandatory report with the NSW Law Society Professional Standards Department under s149 Legal Profession Uniform Law (NSW), disclosing the qualified audit findings. The Law Society opens file LS-2024-0089 and appoints a trust account investigator. The report identifies Thomas Nguyen as the sole administrator with access to the affected accounts during the relevant period. The Law Society refers the matter to NSW Police Financial Crimes Squad on 11 January 2024.

subject: NSW Police Financial Crimes Squad — Investigation E2024/0447
summary: Detective Sergeant Priya Mehta (Financial Crimes Squad) assigned as OIC — investigation designated E2024/0447
content: NSW Police Financial Crimes Squad, State Crime Command, opens Investigation E2024/0447. Detective Sergeant Priya Mehta is designated Officer in Charge. Initial investigative steps include: (1) restraining order application filed under s19 Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 over the Coastal Advisory and TN Consulting bank accounts; (2) production orders issued to Commonwealth Bank, ANZ, and NAB for 24 months of transaction records; (3) forensic imaging of Pinnacle Legal Partners' server undertaken by Police Cyber Crime Squad; (4) LEAP software provider (InfoTrack) served with a preservation notice. DS Mehta estimates 180+ individual fraudulent transactions across the investigation period.

subject: CBA and ANZ production orders satisfied — forensic accounting commences
summary: Bank records confirm $480,240 transferred to shell company accounts controlled by Nguyen across 47 transactions
content: Commonwealth Bank and ANZ satisfy production orders. Police forensic accountant Senior Constable David Park completes initial analysis: 47 transactions totalling $480,240 are identified flowing from Pinnacle Legal Partners client trust account to Coastal Advisory Pty Ltd (CBA BSB 062-000) and TN Consulting Services Pty Ltd (ANZ BSB 012-345). Funds were subsequently withdrawn in cash or transferred to personal accounts held in Thomas Nguyen's name and the name of his de facto partner, Linh Tran. Park's report identifies the scheme as a 'disbursement coding fraud' — a known typology used in professional services trust account fraud.

subject: Search warrants executed at Nguyen's Chatswood residence and office
summary: Police seize laptops, phones, financial documents, and $28,400 cash from residential search
content: Search warrants under s49 Law Enforcement (Powers and Responsibilities) Act 2002 (NSW) are executed at: (1) 14 Archer Street, Chatswood NSW 2067 (residential — attended by 6 officers); (2) Level 12, 1 Market Street, Sydney NSW 2000 (Pinnacle Legal Partners office). Items seized from the residence include: MacBook Pro (serial SN-MBP-2022-4471), Samsung Galaxy S23 (IMEI 352017112345678), 47 pages of handwritten financial notes, bank statements for 6 accounts, and $28,400 cash in two envelopes. Nguyen is present during the residential search and declines to answer questions.

subject: Thomas Michael Nguyen arrested — charged with 3 counts fraud s192E Crimes Act 1900
summary: Nguyen arrested at Chatswood Police Station, charged on Court Attendance Notice — refused bail by police
content: Thomas Michael Nguyen (DOB 14/04/1981, of 14 Archer Street, Chatswood) is arrested at 09:15 AM at Chatswood Police Station. He is charged by Court Attendance Notice with: (1) Fraud — obtain financial advantage by deception s192E(1)(b) Crimes Act 1900 (NSW) — 47 transactions, total value $480,240 [Count 1, specimen charge]; (2) Deal with proceeds of crime (s193B(2) Crimes Act 1900 — Coastal Advisory account); (3) Deal with proceeds of crime (s193B(2) Crimes Act 1900 — TN Consulting account). Maximum penalty: s192E — 10 years imprisonment. Police bail refused. Nguyen is taken to the Downing Centre cells to appear in court the following morning.

event_type: First Mention — Downing Centre Local Court
subject: First mention — Downing Centre Local Court, Magistrate Singh
summary: Bail application adjourned to 14 March — Legal Aid NSW duty solicitor appears — charge details read
content: Matter first mentioned before Magistrate S. Singh at Downing Centre Local Court (Court 7.1). Thomas Nguyen appears in custody via AVL from the Silverwater Correctional Complex. Legal Aid NSW duty solicitor Alexandra Petrov appears for the defendant. The prosecution is represented by Police Prosecutor Sergeant Kim Wong. Charges are formally read. Bail application is made and adjourned to 14 March 2024 to allow the defence to prepare a formal bail application with surety evidence. Nguyen is remanded in custody to Silverwater Correctional Complex. The prosecution opposes bail on flight risk and evidence interference grounds.

subject: Bail granted — $250,000 surety, passport surrendered, daily reporting to Chatswood Police
summary: Magistrate Obi grants bail with conditions: $250,000 surety (parents), surrender passport, report daily, reside at Chatswood address, not approach Pinnacle Legal Partners premises
content: Bail hearing before Magistrate J. Obi, Downing Centre Local Court. Nguyen is now represented by solicitor Marcus Webb of Webb Criminal Law. Surety of $250,000 is offered by Nguyen's parents, Minh and Huong Nguyen (proprietors of Nguyen's Pharmacy, Cabramatta). Bail is granted on the following conditions: (1) reside at 14 Archer Street, Chatswood; (2) report daily to Chatswood Police Station before 10:00 AM; (3) surrender passport (Vietnamese and Australian) to NSW Police; (4) not approach within 500m of Pinnacle Legal Partners offices (1 Market Street, Sydney) or contact any current or former employee of the firm; (5) not travel interstate without leave of court. Prosecution does not oppose bail on these terms. Nguyen is released on 14 March 2024 at 3:45 PM.

subject: Committal mention — defence elects for full committal hearing
summary: Defence elects for committal hearing — brief served by prosecution — hearing listed for 22 July 2024
content: Committal mention before Magistrate T. Browning, Downing Centre Local Court. The prosecution serves the full hand-up brief (342 pages) including: police facts, forensic accounting report, CCTV footage from Pinnacle Legal Partners, digital forensics report from the Cyber Crime Squad, bank records for 8 accounts, and 14 witness statements. Solicitor Marcus Webb elects for a full committal hearing (rather than a hand-up committal) on the basis that the defence intends to cross-examine forensic accountant SC David Park and BDO auditor Rebecca Okafor regarding the methodology underlying the $480,240 calculation. Matter is listed for committal hearing on 22 July 2024 (3 days).

subject: Committal hearing commences — cross-examination of forensic accountant SC Park
summary: Defence cross-examines SC Park on 3 disputed transactions totalling $41,200 — Park maintains methodology is sound
content: Committal hearing commences before Magistrate T. Browning (3 days allocated). Day 1: Forensic accountant SC David Park gives evidence. Under cross-examination by Marcus Webb, Park is challenged on 3 transactions totalling $41,200 which the defence argues may represent legitimate disbursements that were incorrectly coded. Park acknowledges he relied on Pinnacle Legal Partners' coding records but maintains that the absence of any invoice or receipt — confirmed by BDO — means the transactions cannot be legitimate. Webb also challenges the chain of custody for the Commonwealth Bank records. Park is unshaken in cross-examination. The matter is stood over to Day 2.

subject: Nguyen committed for trial to NSW District Court on all 3 counts
summary: Magistrate Browning finds prima facie case established on all counts — committed to District Court
content: Following completion of the committal hearing (Days 2-3: BDO auditor Rebecca Okafor gives evidence; digital forensics expert Sergeant Lim gives evidence re LEAP audit trail tampering), Magistrate T. Browning finds a prima facie case on all three counts and commits Thomas Nguyen for trial to the NSW District Court. The matter is referred to the District Court Registry, Darlinghurst. The prosecution's total quantified loss is maintained at $480,240 across 47 transactions. Nguyen's bail conditions are continued.

subject: Arraignment before Judge Reilly — District Court, Darlinghurst — plea: not guilty
summary: Nguyen arraigned before Her Honour Judge P. Reilly — pleads not guilty to all 3 counts — trial listed for 3 March 2025
content: Thomas Nguyen is arraigned before Her Honour Judge P. Reilly SC at the NSW District Court, Darlinghurst (Court 1). He enters pleas of not guilty to all three counts. Trial is listed to commence on 3 March 2025 with an estimate of 10 days. A pre-trial directions hearing is listed for 15 November 2024. Nguyen is represented by barrister Gabrielle Hartmann SC (briefed by Webb Criminal Law). The Crown is represented by Crown Prosecutor James Callahan SC. Bail conditions are continued. Judge Reilly notes the case involves complex documentary evidence and directs parties to file agreed facts and objections to evidence by 1 February 2025.

subject: Pre-trial directions — defence files s137 Evidence Act objections to 14 LEAP system records
summary: Defence objects to admissibility of LEAP audit logs on chain of custody grounds — Crown to respond by 20 December 2024
content: Pre-trial directions hearing before Judge P. Reilly. Defence counsel Gabrielle Hartmann SC files objections under s137 Evidence Act 1995 (Cth) to 14 LEAP system audit log records, arguing their probative value is outweighed by the danger of unfair prejudice given uncertainty about whether the logs were complete or selectively exported by police. The Crown maintains the logs were extracted under forensic protocol. Judge Reilly orders: (1) Crown to file a response by 20 December 2024; (2) Parties to file agreed facts by 1 February 2025; (3) Jury empanelment directions to be addressed at a further hearing on 14 February 2025.

subject: Parties file 38-page agreed facts document — 31 of 47 transactions not disputed
summary: Crown and defence agree on 31 of 47 transactions as fraudulent — 16 transactions (totalling $89,300) remain contested
content: Parties file agreed facts pursuant to Judge Reilly's directions. Key agreed facts: (1) Nguyen was employed as Senior Accountant at Pinnacle Legal Partners from 4 June 2019 to 8 January 2024; (2) Nguyen had sole administrator access to the LEAP disbursements module throughout the relevant period; (3) 31 of 47 identified transactions (totalling $390,940) cannot be matched to any legitimate disbursement; (4) Coastal Advisory Pty Ltd and TN Consulting Services Pty Ltd were both incorporated by Nguyen in 2022; (5) Nguyen's personal bank accounts received funds from both shell companies. The parties do not agree that the remaining 16 transactions (totalling $89,300) were fraudulent — this is the live issue for trial.

subject: Trial commences before Judge Reilly and jury of 12 — Crown opens
summary: Crown opens to jury — case framed around Nguyen's exclusive access, shell company structure, and pattern of cash withdrawals
content: Trial commences at 10:00 AM before Her Honour Judge P. Reilly SC and a jury of 12. Crown Prosecutor James Callahan SC opens the Crown case. Opening narrative: 'The accused used his position of trust to systematically steal from his employer's clients over 22 months. He did not do this once or twice — he did it 47 times. He constructed shell companies, he falsified records, and he withdrew the cash. This is a case about greed and systematic dishonesty.' The defence opening (Hartmann SC) focuses on the 16 disputed transactions and challenges the reliability of the LEAP audit logs. Jury is directed to approach each count separately.

subject: Crown closes after 7 days — 11 witnesses called including SC Park, Okafor, and digital forensics
summary: Crown calls 11 witnesses over 7 days — Judge Reilly rejects s137 objections to LEAP logs — all 14 audit records admitted
content: The Crown closes its case after calling 11 witnesses over 7 trial days. Key witnesses: (1) SC David Park (forensic accountant) — confirmed $480,240 total; (2) Rebecca Okafor (BDO) — confirmed qualified audit findings; (3) Sergeant Andrew Lim (Cyber Crime Squad digital forensics) — gave evidence that LEAP logs showed 9 instances of back-dated entry modification consistent with covering tracks; (4) Christine Ellard (Managing Partner) — confirmed Nguyen was the sole authorised administrator; (5) 3 current Pinnacle employees who identified their signatures as having been forged on disbursement authorisation forms. Judge Reilly rules against the s137 objections — all 14 LEAP audit records admitted.

subject: Nguyen elects to give evidence — cross-examined for 2.5 days by Crown Prosecutor Callahan SC
summary: Nguyen denies knowledge of shell companies — claims Linh Tran (de facto partner) handled his personal finances — Crown puts 31 agreed transactions to him directly
content: Nguyen elects to give evidence in his own defence. Examination-in-chief by Hartmann SC (3 hours): Nguyen denies creating Coastal Advisory or TN Consulting; claims his de facto partner Linh Tran established the companies for a planned import business; denies any knowledge of the transfers. Cross-examination by Callahan SC (2.5 days): Crown puts to Nguyen that his ABN is listed as sole director of both companies; his personal mobile number is the registered contact for both ABNs; bank records show he made all cash withdrawals personally; CCTV footage from ANZ Chatswood shows him withdrawing $27,000 over 3 days in December 2023. Nguyen maintains he 'cannot explain' the records. Defence case closes.

subject: Closing addresses — Crown 3 hours, Defence 4 hours — Judge Reilly sums up on 21 March
summary: Crown: 'The evidence is overwhelming — 47 transactions, shell companies, cash, forged signatures.' Defence: 'Reasonable doubt exists on 16 transactions — acquit on those counts at minimum.'
content: Closing addresses delivered. Crown Prosecutor Callahan SC (3 hours): 'The accused had the access, the motive, and the means. His own name is on the company registrations. His face is on the CCTV. His account received the money. There is no innocent explanation — none was offered.' Defence counsel Hartmann SC (4 hours): Concedes the 31 agreed transactions but argues the 16 remaining transactions have innocent explanations consistent with legitimate coding errors; urges the jury to apply the Liberato direction strictly; submits that the Crown has not excluded reasonable doubt on the proceeds of crime counts because the jury cannot be satisfied the disputed $89,300 derived from fraud. Judge Reilly delivers the summing up on 21 March (5 hours).

subject: Jury deliberates 2 days — guilty on all 3 counts
summary: Jury returns guilty verdicts on all 3 counts after 14 hours deliberation — Nguyen remanded in custody for sentencing
content: After 14 hours of deliberation over 2 days, the jury returns verdicts of GUILTY on all three counts: (1) Fraud — obtain financial advantage by deception (s192E(1)(b) Crimes Act 1900) — total value $480,240; (2) Deal with proceeds of crime — Coastal Advisory account (s193B(2)); (3) Deal with proceeds of crime — TN Consulting account (s193B(2)). Nguyen shows no visible reaction to the verdicts. Hartmann SC applies for bail pending sentence to allow Nguyen to put his affairs in order; the Crown opposes. Judge Reilly remands Nguyen in custody to the Metropolitan Remand and Reception Centre, Silverwater, and lists sentencing for 28 April 2025. A pre-sentence report is ordered.

subject: Sentence — 4 years 6 months, non-parole 2 years 9 months — earliest release 24 December 2027
summary: Her Honour Judge Reilly imposes 4 years 6 months imprisonment with non-parole period of 2 years 9 months — earliest release date 24 December 2027
content: Sentence delivered by Her Honour Judge P. Reilly SC. Objective seriousness: above mid-range. Aggravating factors (s21A(2) Crimes (Sentencing Procedure) Act 1999): (1) serious planned criminal enterprise over 22 months; (2) significant breach of position of trust; (3) value of $480,240 substantially above the range for ordinary fraud; (4) no prior conviction, however no discount available given not guilty plea. Mitigating factors: (1) no prior criminal history; (2) difficult family circumstances raised in pre-sentence report; (3) prospects of rehabilitation assessed as moderate. Total sentence: 4 years 6 months. Non-parole period: 2 years 9 months. Sentence commences 24 March 2025 (day of remand). Earliest release date: 24 December 2027. Forfeiture orders made over Coastal Advisory and TN Consulting accounts ($391,440 recovered — $88,800 unrecovered). Nguyen is to be placed on the NSW professional disqualification register.
